A man in a red shirt is initially about 6–8 m ahead and slightly left of centre, facing generally toward the camera wearer; across the five frames he approaches or is approached until he is roughly 1 m away, shifts to the right side of the view, and becomes partly cropped and motion-blurred. Several other people remain farther away, approximately 4–10 m ahead around or behind the counters; most are separated from the red-shirted man by about 3–7 m, and at least one appears to face toward the aisle while clear eye direction is not visible. The nearest shelves and the right-side wall edge are within roughly 1–2 m of the camera wearer, while the distant counters, refrigerators, and people are outside arm's reach; the red-shirted man enters approximate arm's reach only in the final frame. Shelving intermittently occludes the lower bodies of the distant people, and the close man increasingly blocks the central-right background as he grows larger in the image.
